title: When the Protocol Burns
premise: Gideon Quintana, a terraformer tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, discovers their own name on the manifest of the Meridian's Grace — a ship that officially never flew and whose passengers were never born. Following the ghost manifest across silent relay stations, Gideon uncovers evidence that an entire generation ship was erased from every record after its crew was massacred, and that they themselves are one of its erased children. To prove the massacre happened, Gideon must broadcast the ship's buried black box from the garden itself, sacrificing the terraforming project they've spent their life building; in doing so, they trade inheritance for truth and finally claim a belonging no registry can grant or revoke.
about_author: Beatrix Blackwood is the pen name of a former orbital agriculture engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop ecosystems for deep-space habitats before turning to fiction. They write about people who tend living things in dead places, and about the paperwork that decides who counts as real.

chapters.title: The Garden of Unborn Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. While logging seed viability in the terraforming dome on quiet station Halcyon Reach, Gideon runs a routine manifest audit and finds their own name listed aboard the Meridian's Grace, a vessel with no flight history and no registered builder. The emotional beat is uncanny displacement: the self they've carefully built begins to feel like someone else's paperwork.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, alternating with intercepted logs from the Grace's quartermaster. Traveling the long route between worlds that no longer speak, Gideon finds witnesses who remember the ship but records that punish remembering. A retired dockmaster slips them a corrupted data shard. The beat hardens from doubt into defiance: Gideon stops asking whether the massacre happened and starts asking who benefits from the lie.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV at climax. Cornered by corporate auditors at Halcyon Reach, Gideon realizes the only transmitter powerful enough to broadcast the restored black box is the garden's own atmospheric seeder network. Using it will cook the seedbeds meant for the unborn colonists. In a brutal choice between legacy and truth, Gideon burns the garden and sends the massacre screaming across every open channel.

chapters.title: Belonging Without a Registry
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, weeks later. The broadcast cannot be un-sent: investigations begin, the erased families are named, and Gideon learns the other children of the Grace survived as scattered orphans like them. Standing in the scorched dome planting the first new seeds by hand, Gideon grieves what was lost and accepts a family found rather than assigned. The beat is quiet, earned belonging.
